messages.author: c364ecf42e3a2785
messages.subject: Error Message Regarding Sample Effort
parts:
Hi everybody,

I'm working on my undergrad thesis and have been running into a couple problems with the program, so I'm hoping more experienced folks can help me out.

I keep receiving the error message: Invalid or missing value for sample effort: 0.0000000.

This occurs when I attempt to run any of my study species through any of the models I'm using (all of CDS and MCDS cosine, with season as a covariate in MCDS). I assume it has something to do with my dataset itself, but I'm not sure exactly what that problem would be. Does anyone have any ideas?

Thanks!

Cate

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Error Message Regarding Sample Effort
parts:
Cate:

I think you're probably correct that your data are not properly organised for Distance to analyse.  Your description is a little sketchy, for example you have not specified whether you are using Distance standalone program (with graphical interface) or Distance in R (I'm guessing the former).  Also not clear whether you have line or point transect data (again I'm assuming the former).

Based upon the two assumptions I am making, the line transect data you have in Distance needs to have a field named "Line length" in the layer named "Line transect".  "Line length" field informs Distance of the length of transect walked; this can also be thought of as the amount of effort exerted by the observer in that portion of the study area.

Best advice is for you to examine any of the "Sample datasets" that are shipped with the Distance programme; specifically the project "Line Transect Example" (if my assumptions are correct).  Also work through Chapter 3--Getting Started of the Distance Users Guide (also shipped with Distance).

If the above is not pertinent to your situation, please ask again with further details.

I was not the only one to enter my data, and so it seems there were a couple occasions where the field was left blank in the original data set that I had to rectify. It was my own oversight, and I'll be sure to go through everything more carefully next time.
